text:
Colorado and Montreal arrive a day and a half apart in the same bad way: both lost or nearly lost in the last minutes of their last game, and both are missing a star. The Avalanche dropped a 4-3 overtime decision in Ottawa on Shane Pinto's goal after the Senators trailed in the third, and they're without Josh Manson and Zachary L'Heureux. The Canadiens beat Boston 5-2, ending the Bruins' four-game winning streak, to extend a run of points in twelve straight (9-0-3), though without Ivan Demidov (ankle) they've leaned on Cole Caufield, who has moved onto Juraj Slafkovský's line, and on Zachary Bolduc, who has moved onto the first power-play unit.

Our numbers see an even game, with expected goals (the quality of chances) at 3.27 for COL and 2.96 for MTL. Montreal's results are ahead of its chances (49% of the expected goals), and goaltending is doing the lifting. Projected starter Jacob Fowler is +13.5 goals saved above expected, against +1.0 for Colorado's Mackenzie Blackwood. The special-teams matchup to watch is Colorado's power play (0.81 expected goals a game) against a Montreal penalty kill that allows 0.82, with MTL taking nearly five penalties a game.

We have Nathan MacKinnon at 37% to score and 81% for a point; he went first overall in 2013. Caufield is at 36% to score, riding a five-game point streak. Our under-the-radar pick is Gabriel Landeskog, a third-line forward with 3.2 expected goals in his last 10 games, at 22% to score. He's a player to watch, not a lock.
